title: Quadratic time for trajectory recording
statement: For every finite-state Boolean machine $M$, Boolean word $y$, natural number $T$, and family of four Boolean words $(k_i)_{i<4}$, form the input $x$ by packing the machine's initial recorder tape contents for $y$ and $T$, together with the four words $k_i$, as self-delimiting fields. The output machine computes the list of recorded counter rows through time $T$ from $x$ in at most $\bigl(10+10((\mathrm{recorder\ tape\ count})+4)+(8(\mathrm{field\ count})+7)\bigr)(|x|+1)^2$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: A family of four Boolean words
replaced: For every source machine, virtual input $y$, horizon $T$, and retained fields, the trajectory-output machine computes the inclusive trajectory from the packed layout within a constant times the square of the encoded argument length plus one; every initial word and the unary horizon occur inside the argument, so the bound covers a zero horizon as well.
